text:
incident-bot: ALERT p99 latency exceeded on dedicated-pool-us-west-2 (model=redwood-3b-q4). p99=8.3s (threshold 3s). Queue growth; streaming stalls observed. Auto-scaler reports delay. Paging on-call.

Amelia (oncall-sre): paging @jay @taylor @priya — I'm getting several alerts: streaming timeouts and tail spikes. Queue depth climbing fast. Can runtime/sre confirm?

Jay (eng-runtime): Looking. Pool desired=50 running=33, many slots in WARMUP. Handshake RTTs look high (~10-13s). Handshake failures correlating with scale events.

Priya (eng-sre): Metrics: queue_depth went 20 -> ~1k in ~3 minutes. warmup_fail_rate around 24%. p95 1.4s, p99 8.3s.

Taylor (serving-runtime): Noted a rollout at 02:12 UTC that adjusted handshake backoff parameters (reduce retry aggressiveness). Possible interaction with recently evicted KV entries — cold KV lookups amplify warmup.

Amelia (oncall-sre): Starting incident bridge — https://call.redwood/bridge/7701239876. @channel please join if you're oncall for runtime or infra.

ops-bot: BRIDGE_CREATED bridge/7701239876. Auto-attach logs stream.

Sara (support): CS reports two enterprise customers saw partial streaming responses followed by timeouts. One flagged as severity-high. CSM @leo has been notified.

Leo (customer-success): I'll message the customer with a short note: "We're investigating elevated streaming latency and may route critical traffic to a hosted fallback temporarily. We'll confirm before taking action." Waiting on confirmation.

Jay (eng-runtime): Initiating manual scale to relieve queued requests: set desired=80 (was 50). Sending scale request now.

ops-bot: ACTION scale_request submitted (id scale-7701239876-1) -> desired=80.

Priya (eng-sre): Host telemetry shows heartbeat misses for the autoscaler agent at 02:18-02:20 UTC, correlated with NTP jitter on a subset of hosts. Several autoscaler decisions deferred.

Taylor (serving-runtime): Warmup latency per slot jumped from ~350ms -> ~5.8s. KV miss ratio increased sharply. Logs show repeated kv-populate-timeout and slot-init retries.

Amelia (oncall-sre): Emergency mitigation options: 1) route affected enterprise customers to hosted fallback model, 2) temporarily revert handshake backoff rollout, 3) aggressive KV prefix prepopulation for priority routes. Thoughts?

Taylor (serving-runtime): Recommend revert + prepopulate first; rerouting can be done per-customer if they approve. Revert should take effect fast.

Jay (eng-runtime): I'll apply the prepopulate flag to enterprise/priority routes and restart slot-init on nodes with stuck WARMUP slots. Doing both now.

devex-bot: Revert rollout rb-7701239876-backoff started. Deploy status: in_progress -> applying to 8 hosts.

ops-bot: COMMAND restart_slot_init executed on nodes [i-0a12,b-0c34,e-0f56].

Priya (eng-sre): After restarts, ~16 slots freed from stuck WARMUP state. warmup_success_rate improving to ~68%.

Jay (eng-runtime): Prepopulation applied to routes tagged enterprise/priority. Starting to see first warmed slots with KV populated.

Amelia (oncall-sre): Any customer approvals for hosted fallback?

Leo (customer-success): One customer (cust-7812) approved fallback for critical routes. They asked about potential context differences — they consented.

Jay (eng-runtime): Implemented route override: cust-7812, cust-4401 -> hosted redwood-3b-std at 02:31 UTC. route-override id ro-7701239876-1.

ops-bot: ROUTE_UPDATE applied for 2 routes.

Priya (eng-sre): Tail metrics for those customers: p99 dropped from ~10s -> ~900ms after reroute. Great signal that routing helps while pool recovers.

Taylor (serving-runtime): The revert completed on 8/8 hosts. Warmup latencies falling — avg_warmup_ms now ~1.1s (was ~5.8s). global p99 down to ~1.9s but still shaving off queued work.

Amelia (oncall-sre): Good. Keep scale to desired=80 until queues drain. Watch for oscillation or flapping.

Priya (eng-sre): Queue depth trending: 1024 -> 230 -> 60 over 10 minutes. p99 now 1.05s. Streaming stalls count dropping.

Sara (support): Communicated to customers: "We've routed critical traffic temporarily and are restoring dedicated capacity. You may notice minor differences in output; we'll share an RCA once complete."

Leo (customer-success): Customer thanked us and requested timeline for formal RCA. We'll coordinate.

Taylor (serving-runtime): Root cause hypothesis: combination of (a) handshake backoff parameter change that reduced aggressive retries during warmup, (b) transient host NTP jitter causing autoscaler heartbeats to miss, and (c) aggressive KV eviction leading to cold-paths on many slots — together amplified warmup times during a burst.

Jay (eng-runtime): Follow-ups we should create: healthcheck improvements for slot-init, circuit-breakers for kv-client to fail fast, autoscaler heartbeat watch alerts, and an e2e chaos test for NTP jitter + KV eviction. I'll file tickets.

Amelia (oncall-sre): Please list follow-ups in this thread. Also tagging severity S2 for incident. We'll keep bridge open 30m for monitoring.

devex-bot: Tickets created: TICKET-7910 (slot-init healthchecks), TICKET-7911 (kv-client circuit-breaker), TICKET-7912 (autoscaler-heartbeat-alert), TICKET-7913 (chaos-ntp-kv-test).

Priya (eng-sre): Note to postmortem: autoscaler missed-window 02:18-02:21 due to host-level NTP drift; investigate host provisioning and NTP config drift.

Taylor (serving-runtime): Recommend adding a sliding warmup concurrency limiter so that when a sudden burst causes many cold slot inits, we don't overload the KV population path and let slots warm in controlled batches.

Amelia (oncall-sre): Agreed. Add that to follow-ups. I'll draft a postmortem and schedule follow-up meeting with eng-runtime, eng-sre, infra, and devex.

ops-bot: INCIDENT_UPDATE severity=S2 -> mitigated. incident duration=18m. Bridge will stay open for 30m.

Sara (support): Notifying affected customers with mitigation summary + next steps.

Leo (customer-success): I'll handle customer comms and coordinate the RCA delivery.

Jay (eng-runtime): Marking this thread done for live mitigation. Will follow up with ticket updates.

Amelia (oncall-sre): Closing page at 02:50 UTC. If any regression, re-pager. End of thread."
